correctness.rationale: The bijection between corona maximal independent sets and independent core sets with one private representative per unchosen cluster is exact. Independent continuous priorities give independent Bernoulli hub candidates and iid cluster-minimum times; the latter are independent of candidate identities. Core-greedy selection on the induced candidate graph follows because a candidate hub can only be blocked by a previously accepted core neighbour. Private winners are independent exchangeable labels conditional on the core outcome, so total variation reduces to the core distribution. The all-private event gives a strict partition-function comparison precisely for cores with edges. Formal Taylor coefficients: empty discrepancy |E(H)|t^2, singleton discrepancy deg(v)t^2/2, and all multi-hub discrepancy O_H(t^3). The handshake lemma yields the sharp |E(H)|/s^2 coefficient. Equalities in the complete-core case are exact by symmetry. For heterogeneous blocks only the independently proven all-private argument is asserted. An independent direct permutation implementation compared 24 graph/size cases and 1,418,450 full orders using exact rational probabilities; all passed. No finite computation is used to prove the infinite statements.

originality.rationale: Full-text checks distinguish the October 2026 tree-only obstruction and spider probabilities from arbitrary clique-corona marginal laws, strict rigidity, and a universal edge-count asymptotic. Kryven–Versendaal–de Vries Proposition 3.8 gives only a sufficient regular-independent-set uniformity criterion, and its 2-uniform-graph classification is neither a converse for arbitrary graphs nor a small-activity total-variation calculation. Krivelevich and coauthors focus on expected greedy-set sizes and local graph limits. Relevant indexed exact greedy-output results concern threshold and chain graphs; the clique-corona indexed result concerns general-position polynomials. A private same-week claim about clique coronas concerns limited domination, not random-greedy MIS; another about clique bouquets concerns a different join graph. The exact claim is not an immediate corollary of these statements. No matching stronger/equivalent published result was identified after semantic, alias, parameter, and full-text comparisons. Priority uncertainty remains.
residual_risks: Similar coupling or edge-count small-activity coefficient may appear in unindexed random-sequential-adsorption, hard-core-model, or stochastic graph-corona literature.
Database and web non-hits are not a proof of novelty or a substitute for independent literature review.
The independently evaluated complete paper texts are restricted to cited sources; closest indexed threshold/chain results were compared at abstract/claim level only.

value.rationale: The result gives a structural law for a natural infinite graph operation over arbitrary finite base graphs and a sharp necessary/sufficient uniformity classification. The all-private event links stochastic greediness to the independence polynomial (hard-core partition function), while a second-order cancellation yields a universal coefficient equal to the core edge count. This is a mathematically motivated new invariant calculation with a meaningful asymptotic law and explicit sharp complete-core examples, not merely a particular small computation or a known-table restatement.
